## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/popover ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/popover"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; export function SharePopover() { return ( }>Share Share this project Anyone with the link can read it, nobody can edit it.

The motion follows the anchor, not the side: the panel grows from `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger. ```tsx … ``` ## With a form The panel is a normal container, so `Field` and `Input` work inside it. Nothing traps focus: a popover is non-modal by default. ```tsx Rename this view Name ``` ## Controlled ```tsx const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); … ; ``` ## Modal when it has to be A popover that holds a destructive control can trap focus and block the page behind it without becoming a dialog: ```tsx }>Danger zone … ``` ## When to use - A small set of controls that belongs to the thing it is attached to: column visibility, a filter, a share link, a colour picker. - Context that would crowd the page if it were always visible, but that the user opens on demand. - An edit that is scoped to one trigger and can be dismissed without losing the page. ## When not to use - A confirmation that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`: a popover can be dismissed by clicking away. - A task that needs the whole screen or a focus trap. Use `dialog` or `sheet`. - A one- or two-word hint on a control. Use `tooltip`, which cannot hold interactive content. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `Popover` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. Non-modal by default. | | `PopoverTrigger` | native button props, `render` | The anchor and the toggle. | | `PopoverContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal and positioner; `sideOffset` defaults to `4`. | | `PopoverHeader` | `className` | Stacked title and description. | | `PopoverTitle` | `className` | Base UI heading; the panel's accessible name. | | `PopoverDescription` | `className` | Muted supporting text; becomes `aria-describedby`. | `PopoverContent` positions itself; there is no `PopoverAnchor` export, because Base UI anchors to the trigger and upstream's Base UI surface has no anchor part. ## Motion contract | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes | | exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) | | reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – | The panel grows out of its anchor rather than sliding towards it. A slide would need a distance token and four per-side classes, and it moves the edge the positioner just lined up away from the trigger; `--transform-origin` says the same thing with one transform. The scale reads `--motion-scale-in`, so the class list carries a token and not a number. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Enter / Space | Opens the popover from its trigger. | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and then out of it; focus is not trapped unless `modal`. | | Escape | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. | Pressing outside closes it, which is the difference between a popover and an alert dialog. ## Accessibility - Base UI gives the popup `role="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` on the trigger, `aria-controls`, and focus return on close. The panel is labelled by `PopoverTitle` and described by `PopoverDescription` when both are rendered. - The trigger keeps `aria-expanded` in step, so assistive technology announces "collapsed" / "expanded" rather than a dialog appearing out of nowhere. - `PopoverTitle` is optional for an interactive panel, but any popover that opens a region of controls should have one: an unnamed dialog is announced as just "dialog". - Interactive controls inside the panel are reachable: the popover is non-modal, so Tab leaves it and the trigger's focus ring stays where the user left it. ## Responsive behavior The panel is `w-72` wide and flips sides when the trigger has no room above or below; Base UI also shifts it along the cross axis to stay inside the viewport. On a narrow screen it can fill most of the width — pass `className="w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]"` or a max width when the content is wider than the default. ## Performance - One popup tree is mounted only while open; the portal unmounts after the exit transition. - Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript animation loop. Reopening during the exit reverses the fade. ## Notes for AI - Use `popover` for anchored, dismissible content; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be explicit. - Pass the trigger through `render`, not a wrapper: the trigger is what the positioner anchors to and what gets `aria-expanded`. - Do not simulate a modal confirmation with `modal`; it blocks outside interaction but still closes on Escape, which is not what a confirmation promises.
